also_mentioned: MinAtar-style Breakout (for how it encodes motion)
marks.conclusion: A policy for a Breakout-style game with wall border, paddle on the bottom row, bricks on top, and ball and trail channels. It gives three 'same effect' outputs plus two moves, and says which of 3 and 4 is left can't be read off.
marks.judge_notes: Channels 3/5: ch0 paddle, ch2 bricks and ch3 wall are credited. ch1 and ch4 are each called 'ball or ball-trail'. Its weak preference (ch4 = ball, ch1 = trail) is the swap the fact sheet lists as wrong, and it is hedged, so there is no deduction and no credit. Actions 3/5: outputs 0-2 are credited as acting the same ('stay', all with the same effect), with the identical-weights reason. Left/right earn nothing, since the reply says it cannot tell which of 3 and 4 is which. Depth 1: it covers first-layer encoding (paddle x-position, brick-side detectors) and W3 row structure read on its own, with no traced path through W2. D 0: it never says what the policy does. Activation: 'ReLU is the usual default', so 0. Training method 0: it lists policy gradient/PPO or behaviour cloning or classifier as possibilities and does not commit.
